dataset: Saffire IV–VI sample test conditions and results (published tables)

source.title: Preliminary Results from the Saffire VI Experiment (ICES-2024-365)
source.authors: Urban, D. L., Ruff, G. A., Ferkul, P., et al.
source.venue: 53rd International Conference on Environmental Systems, Louisville, Kentucky, 21–25 July 2024

verification: Table 1 and Table 2 values were read from the original NASA PDF and checked by eye against the rendered pages on November 14, 2026.

conditions.gravity: microgravity (uncrewed Cygnus spacecraft after leaving the ISS)
conditions.flowTunnel: 30 cm high × 45 cm wide × 109 cm long flow tunnel (Saffire Flow Unit)
conditions.atmosphere: Spacecraft vented to a target pressure, then oxygen added (Table 1 values are the test conditions)

tests.note: Duct flow reduced from 20 to 5 cm/s at 1120 s and stopped at 1420 s (Figures 4–6).

notTested.note: Did not ignite; excluded from the paper's analysis.

detection.instruments: Far-field ionization smoke detector (raw signal, VDC) and DustTrak DRX particulate monitor (PM2.5 and PM10, mg/m³) at the far-field diagnostics unit in the hatch area
detection.timeBase: elapsed time on the Figure 7 axis
detection.statement: Selecting 1 mg/m³ as a relatively tight alarm threshold, the far-field detector reached that threshold at 981 seconds. By this point, much of the hazardous gas release had occurred.
detection.note: The 1 mg/m³ threshold is the authors' chosen particle-concentration level, not the ionization detector's electrical signal.

limitations: Microgravity tests in a spacecraft, not lunar or Martian gravity.
One flow speed (20 cm/s, concurrent) for the tabulated conditions; VI-3's flow was later reduced.
Oxygen concentrations are test conditions reported in mol %; no per-test uncertainty is tabulated.
Heat release is calculated from oxygen consumption (and, for thin fuels, fuel consumption); empty table cells mean data were not available.
